title.title: Uniform black-box noncommutative identity testing
title.subtitle: Claim: one explicit matrix tuple of dimension at most $2ns^2$ catches every nonzero size-$s$ formula

plain: Plug one fixed set of matrices into any small formula: if it is not secretly zero, the answer shows it

beats.text: In noncommuting variables, $xy - yx$ is a nonzero formula
Plug in numbers and it vanishes; plug in matrices and it need not
Claimed: one explicit tuple, dimension at most $2ns^2$, catches every nonzero size-$s$ formula

steps: Encode each word as a nested integral in one variable
Different words give independent results, so none cancel
A small formula cannot vanish too deeply at zero
So a short slice, written as matrices, still sees it

achievement.label: Polynomial-size black-box hitting sets (open)
achievement.context: Before: quasipolynomial hitting sets for noncommutative ABPs (Forbes–Shpilka, 2013)
achievement.note: Entries have bit length $O(n s^2 \log n)$: polynomial, but heavy

verify.detail: In Lean: the universal hitting property only, not the bit-time or dimension bounds
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: One test point for every formula.
With numbers, x y minus y x vanishes. With matrices, it need not.
Each word becomes its own integral, so no two can cancel.
Claimed: one small matrix tuple suffices.

sources.quote: one rational matrix tuple of dimension <= 2ns^2 on which every nonzero size-s noncommutative formula in n variables over any characteristic-zero field is nonzero
Forbes-Shpilka (FOCS 2013) quasipolynomial black-box hitting sets for noncommutative ABPs
Matrix entries have bit length O(n s^2 log n), so a single test is polynomial but heavy.
FormulaHitting.lean (universal hitting property only; bit-time and dimension bounds not asserted)
